To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in rats fed high NaCl diets from weaning central AT1 and central AT2 receptors are involved in AII-induced drinking while in rats fed normal NaCl diets from the same age the AT1 receptor plays a more prominent role.
central AT1 and A12 receptors mediate chronic ICV AIl-induced drinking in high sodium chloride diet rats from weaning.

chronic ICV AIl-induced drinking in rats on high sodium chloride diet was mediated by both AT1 and AT1 receptors, while in normal sodium fed rats AIl stimulated central AT1 receptors to induce drinking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the brain angiotensin system in the regulation of body fluid homeostasis.
the role of brain angiotensin receptors in the regulation of drinking behavior.
the role of central AII receptors in mediating the drinking response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AT1 receptor is the primary receptor for AII in the central regulation of sodium intake, but the AT2 receptor may also contribute in some conditions.
the chronic central AII-induced drinking response is mediated by both central AT1 receptors and AT2 receptors.
the central AT1 receptor plays a major role in mediating chronic intracerebral AII-induced drinking, but that the AT2 receptor is also involved in the process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the normal sodium diet fed rats, AII stimulates central AT1 receptors to induce drinking while in the high sodium diet fed rats the peptide also stimulates central AT2 receptors to mediate drinking.
chronic central angiotensin-II infusion increases water intake in rats raised on a high sodium diet from weaning, and the drinking response is mediated by both AT1 and AT-2 receptors.

chronic ICV AIl infusion in rats fed high NaCl from weaning stimulates both AT1 and AT 2 receptors to induce chronic drinking, while in normal NaCl fed rats the peptide stimulates primarily AT1 receptors to induce chronic AII-induced drinking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the central AT1 and/or AT2 receptors play a major role in the regulation of water balance in rats raised on a high sodium chloride diet.

in rats raised on high sodium chloride diet the AT1 and AT 2 receptors play an equivalent role in mediating AII-induced drinking, while in rats fed normal sodium chloride diet the drinking response to AII is mediated mainly by the AT1 receptors.
in the high sodium chloride-fed animals, chronic ICV A II stimulates both AT1 and AT 2 receptors in the brain to induce drinking.
